businesses.what_they_do: Marriage and family therapy practice of Kenneth Young, PhD, LMFT (25 years), counselling couples, families and individuals with structural family therapy and CBT, integrating clients' faith where requested. Also runs a 12-step based addictions support group and a Newark office.
businesses.customers: Couples, families, teens and individuals, including faith-oriented and multicultural clients; accepts many insurance plans plus sliding scale.

size_signals.signal: Primary office in North Brunswick plus a second location at 326 15th Ave, Newark
Group program (Life Controlling Addictions Support Group, $50-100, twice weekly) in addition to individual sessions
Accepts Aetna, BCBS, Health Net, HealthFirst, Horizon, MHN, UnitedHealthcare and offers sliding scale

website_review.trust_signals: None visible; the domain shows only a page title

website_review.search_basics: No working content: title is "🐴 Multi-Faith Multi-Cultural Counseling Group", meta description empty, no H1, no service pages, no schema

Google listing uses a different name (Multifaith and Multicultural Counseling & Coaching Group) and a different phone (732-317-1902) from the PT profile's (732) 410-7430

agent_readiness.notes: The only 'website' is a frameset that fails, so there is nothing for a crawler to index beyond a title; no robots.txt (404); no schema; Google profile exists with 5.0 from 5 reviews but under a variant name and a different phone number; all service, fee and insurance detail lives on Psychology Today, not on owned pages; nothing bookable.

operations_signals.signal: Two locations plus a twice-weekly support group, with no online scheduling or intake form anywhere the practice controls
Insurance panels and sliding-scale eligibility imply manual verification for every new client
Directory traffic is the only funnel; prospective clients reaching the broken domain bounce

scores.reasons: The business's only website is dead and there is no booking or intake, so the gap is as large as it gets. A solo LMFT with insurance panels and a support group has modest budget; a replacement site plus listing cleanup is a small, fast engagement.

caveats: Google Maps only exposed a limited view: ratings were visible but review counts usually were not, so review volume is understated across the batch.

Several unrelated sites in this batch (Inspire PT, Farrington Pediatrics, Low Vision Center, medispaclinics.com, The Healing Tree, mfmccounselinggroup.com) share the same stray horse emoji at the start of their title tags and similar single-purpose-page structure. Inference: they were built or templated by the same small web vendor, which is a plausible common root cause for the identical metadata and schema gaps.

All ten businesses are small healthcare practices in one town; scores compare them to each other, and ability_to_pay is a judgement from visible signals (single vs multi-provider, insurance panels, published fees), not from financial data.
data_gaps: Google review counts were not rendered in the limited Maps view; only ratings and, for Jordan Psychotherapy, a review count of 9.
